invariants: Numbers run DOWN the first column then down the second, never across. That is how a contents page reads and how anyone hunting for item 11 will look for it.
Dotted rules, not table borders. Sixteen rows with hard rules read as a spreadsheet; the dot system's soft break gives the eye a baseline to jump along.
Part label, title and note sit on three separate baselines. The source sets the last two on one and they print through each other.
Ten to sixteen entries. Below ten a plain column set is better; above sixteen the rows fall under the type floor.
